claim: Senator Marcus Webb announced in a January 2026 floor speech that federal infrastructure spending under the current administration has increased by 47% since 2022.

sources.title: Webb Touts Infrastructure Win on Senate Floor
sources.author: Staff Reporter
sources.summary: Senator Webb delivered remarks on the Senate floor praising the administration's infrastructure record, citing a 47% spending increase since 2022.
sources.claims: Federal infrastructure spending has increased 47% since 2022. Webb credited bipartisan cooperation for the gains. The figure was attributed to an internal Senate Budget Committee briefing.
sources.quotes: We have delivered on our promise to rebuild America — 47 percent more in infrastructure dollars since this administration took office.
sources.context: Shared as primary sourcing for a story about infrastructure claims.

sources.title: Infrastructure Budget Numbers: What the Data Shows
sources.author: Policy Desk
sources.summary: Analysis citing Senator Webb's floor remarks and echoing the 47% figure, sourced to the same Senate Budget Committee briefing document.
sources.claims: The 47% increase figure is consistent with Senate Budget Committee preliminary data. Infrastructure outlays have risen substantially in the 2023-2025 period.
sources.quotes: Preliminary Senate Budget Committee figures support the broad direction of Webb's claim, though exact percentages await final audit.
sources.context: Corroboration source for the 47% infrastructure spending figure.

sources.title: Senator Webb's January Floor Speech — Full Transcript Excerpt
sources.author: Webb Campaign Communications
sources.summary: Webb campaign site publishes an excerpt of the floor speech, repeating the 47% infrastructure spending claim.
sources.claims: Infrastructure investment is up 47% since 2022 per the senator's prepared remarks. The campaign notes this figure comes from the Budget Committee briefing provided to members.
sources.quotes: Infrastructure investment in this country is up 47 percent — that is not a talking point, that is the Budget Committee's own numbers.
sources.context: Third source confirming the specific 47% figure and its attributed provenance.
